summary: An early Telnet option, from 1974, for negotiating what happens when a horizontal tab character is sent to a terminal. The two sides can agree on who handles the tab, for example whether it is passed through or turned into something else. It is historic.

plainLanguage.summary: This Telnet option lets the sender and receiver agree who handles horizontal tab characters in output. It defines several possible actions, including delaying, replacing or discarding a tab.

subtitle: A Telnet option for agreeing how horizontal tab characters are handled in output.

tldr.problem: The sender and receiver need to agree which side handles horizontal tab characters and what handling to apply.
tldr.mechanism: The NAOHTD option uses Telnet negotiation and subnegotiation values to select a handler and a tab disposition.
tldr.outcome: The RFC defines values for delays, replacement, discarding, simulation and other handling, plus rules for choosing the responsible party.

today: RFC 654 is Historic according to the unit metadata. It defines negotiation rules for output horizontal tab disposition.

sections.title: The NAOHTD Option
sections.content:
RFC 654 defines NAOHTD, or Negotiate About Output Horizontal Tab Disposition. The option is for a simplex connection and allows the data sender and receiver to negotiate which party handles output horizontal tab characters.

In the default mode there is no negotiation. Neither party is required or prohibited from handling tabs, though the RFC says it is appropriate for the receiver to handle them at least primitively.
sections.plainLanguage: The option lets the sender and receiver agree how to handle horizontal tabs. Without negotiation, the receiver may handle them in a basic way.

sections.title: Negotiation and Disposition Values
sections.content:
The parties use IAC DO NAOHTD, IAC WILL NAOHTD, IAC DON'T NAOHTD and IAC WON'T NAOHTD to request, accept or refuse negotiation. In subnegotiation, DS (code 1) identifies a sender proposal and DR (code 0) a receiver proposal.

Value 0 means the sender will handle tabs. Values 1 through 250 ask the other party to handle them after a delay measured in character-times or NUL characters. Value 251 replaces a tab with a space, 252 discards it, 253 simulates tabbing, 254 waits for a character on the opposite simplex connection, and 255 leaves the handling method unspecified.
sections.plainLanguage: The value says who handles a tab and what to do. Options include adding a delay, replacing the tab with a space, discarding it or simulating its effect.

sections.title: Choosing a Handler
sections.content:
If neither the sender nor receiver wants to handle output tabs, the receiver must do so. If both want to handle them, the sender does, taking the receiver's suggestions into account.

For a delay, the sender inserts NUL characters immediately after the tab. Either party can disable further negotiation with WON'T NAOHTD or DON'T NAOHTD.
sections.plainLanguage: If both parties want to handle tabs, the sender takes responsibility. If neither does, the receiver must handle them.
